title: Geometric composition and exact etale sum-extension
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its specified algebra structure. Use the actual quotient rings $A_n=\mathcal O_E/(\ell)^{n+1}$, the strict coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], their ordinary derived categories [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], and the constructible finite-Tor tower category [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Let $k$ be a field of positive characteristic different from $\ell$. Fix the same $b,o,x$ satisfying Laws of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels], section-normalized tower coordinates q and identity-on-sections finite direct-image coordinates z. There are normalized finite evaluation data and compact-support identity, refinement and composition isomorphisms. Under each preservation hypothesis for compact support on the full constructible finite-Tor tower categories, there is an exact etale sum-extension adjunction, its graph-summand identification with compact support, the cohomological and Tor interval preservation assertions, coherent refinement and composition laws with their canonical finite evaluations, and the open-immersion normalization equation. No coefficient reduction compatibility is asserted. The precise normalization equations are the interfaces FiniteNormalization, CompositionOperations, EtaleCalculus and CompositionCoherence and the displayed open equation in the Lean statement.

proof.text: Use the actual strict semilinear section model of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] with ring system $A_{n,T}$: its ordinary homotopy category is $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$, and it supplies inverse image, separately derived direct image, open extension, their units/counits, and the comparisons built from them. It does not identify a derived morphism with an arbitrary family of its evaluations. Every level of an object of $\mathcal C_T$ has bounded constructible etale origin by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. These representatives have the same Tor intervals by [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]: the schemes are qcqs and $A_n$ is finite, hence discrete Noetherian. Consequently the finite comparisons in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] apply over the arbitrary field $k$ in the statement; no global finite-field datum is needed. We will use [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] to identify evaluations and detect invertibility only after constructing maps in the section model.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition: prerequisites for the tower version; finite constructible comparison is proetale.tex Tag 09AL (lemma-compare-constructible-derived). The enhanced section assertion is the cited node, not a claim of these tags.

proof.text: Construct proper/open comparisons before evaluation. For a commutative square $pk=ir$ with $p,r$ proper and $i,k$ open, put $W'=W\times_T S$ and $s=(k,r):V\to W'$. The geometric clause of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] makes $s$ clopen. The sheafified presheaf of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] gives the open base-change map $\beta:p^*i_!\simeq b_!q^*$. Exactness is [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. The termwise clopen projection defines $\alpha_Q$ and its proper-adjunction mate $\gamma_Q$. Apply [lem-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-pasting]: the projection is ring-linear and commutes with semilinear transitions, so the maps are actual tower transformations; the section model of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] realizes them simultaneously, and its horizontal and vertical identities hold before evaluation by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Evaluation is the finite normalized mate from [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence], hence is invertible on the constructible finite-ring origins supplied in step 1 by [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] and detected by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels].

source.place: Tags 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), 0F7D (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal); ring-system mate construction and coefficient-independent clopen projection calculation are agent supplied.

proof.text: For $T\xrightarrow hB\xrightarrow gC$, choose a compatible compactification tower using [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]. Write $i:B\hookrightarrow\overline B$, $q:\overline B\to C$, $a:T\hookrightarrow\overline T$, $p:\overline T\to\overline B$, and $U=\overline T\times_{\overline B}B$, with $a=bj$ and $r:U\to B$ proper. The comparison applies the proper/open mate from step 2, followed by the inverse of the canonical direct-image compositor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and the open compositor [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. The direct-image compositors are conjugates of the coherent inverse-image compositors, so [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] supplies their identity and associativity laws. Its independence from the chosen tower and its equality for common refinements are exactly [lem-sp-compactification-refinement-coherence], using [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered]; the latter also equalizes parallel refinement arrows. Thus $\alpha_{g,h}$ is well-defined. Applying the same lemma to a three-map staircase gives associativity, while identity towers give identities. Evaluation is the finite construction of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] with the site normalization [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] and is invertible by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. If $u:U\hookrightarrow T$ is open, use $(ju,p)$; [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] gives $F_{hu}=F_hu_!$ and the canonical open counits. The preservation assumption in the statement applies to each proper or open map used here, so these operations restrict to the chosen categories.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), compatible diagram and its displayed four equalities, followed by comparison through a common refining tower; the pasting equations are implemented at tower level in step 2.

proof.text:
For etale $e:U\to T$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$. At each $n$ define $e_!M_n$ by sheafifying
$$V\longmapsto\bigoplus_{t:V\to U\,/T}M_n(V,t),$$
with transition maps induced on each summand by those of $M$. The scalar action factors through $A_n$, so this is an actual functor on varying-coefficient towers. [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] makes $e_!$ and $e^*$ exact; exactness on towers follows from [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. The unit places a section in the summand of its structural lift; the counit sums the evaluations of all lifts. Both commute with the quotient transitions summand by summand. The adjunction bijection is a bijection on compatible families because these unit/counit formulas are natural in the level maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] on complexes and then [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]: exactness lets both functors descend, and the two triangle identities descend with them. This proves $e_{!,\bullet}\dashv e_\bullet^*$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories themselves, not by levelwise conservativity. For an open immersion there is at most one lift, giving extension by zero.

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); explicit tower unit and counit are induced on the summands.

proof.text: Identify the exact sum-extension functor with the compactification candidate by constructing the comparison. For a pro-etale test object $V\to T$, each lift $t:V\to U$ has a graph in $\overline U\times_TV$, closed because $p$ is separated and open because the etale diagonal is open. [lem-sp-varying-ring-graph-summand] constructs the graph section extended by zero, proves its $A_n$-linearity and transition compatibility, and assembles the natural tower map $\theta:e_{!,\bullet}\to F_e$. The localized-site morphism [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] identifies the right adjoints of the etale and pro-etale sum-extension functors, so the site comparison is an isomorphism and preserves units and counits. On each finite etale-origin level, [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility] identifies $\theta_n$ with the inverse finite normalization; [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] gives the coefficient comparison. Hence $\theta$ is invertible by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. The finite counit is the fibre sum by [lem-amb-etale-sum-stalks], and the open case is the unique-lift inclusion. Its coefficient compatibility follows from the graph construction and the last sum-extension identity of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility].

source.place: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale), graph-section map; more-etale.tex Tags 0F4Y (lemma-separated-etale-shriek) and 0GKM (lemma-Rf-shriek-for-quasi-finite), compact-support-to-sum normalization; proetale.tex Tag 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison). The clopen-graph map supplies the strict tower comparison.

proof.text:
Exactness of $e_!$ and $e^*$ gives $H^q(e_!M_n)=e_!H^q(M_n)$ and $H^q(e^*N_n)=e^*H^q(N_n)$, so each cohomological interval is preserved without shifting, uniformly in $n$. For every degree-zero module sheaf $N$ on $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] gives $e_!P\otimes N\cong e_!(P\otimes e^*N)$. It also shows that $e_!$ preserves flat sheaves: tensor an injection with a flat sheaf on $U$, then apply exact $e_!$. Thus applying this identity to K-flat resolutions gives
$$(e_!M_n)\otimes^LN\simeq e_!(M_n\otimes^Le^*N).$$
This preserves every Tor interval. For an arbitrary module sheaf $Q$ on $U$ the structural summand makes $Q$ a direct summand of $e^*e_!Q$: the complementary lifts are the complement of the clopen diagonal of separated $e$. For $L_n$ on $T$ with Tor interval $[a,b]$, $e^*L_n\otimes^LQ$ is a direct summand of
$$e^*(L_n\otimes^Le_!Q),$$
using derived tensor/pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The latter has the required interval by the Tor bound on $L_n$ and exactness of $e^*$, which proves it for $Q$. Constructibility for $e^*$ follows by pulling back the finite partition and the local constant finite presentations. Constructibility for $e_!$ on $\mathcal C_U$ follows from step 5 and the assumed preservation by $F_e$. The ambient adjunction therefore restricts to $\mathcal C_U,\mathcal C_T$ with precisely the same units and counits.

lean.statement:
theorem geometric_calculus
    (pchar : ℕ) (hp : 0 < pchar) (hne : pchar ≠ l)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k pchar]
    (b : SpTowerShriek.Base l E) (o : SpTowerShriek.Operations l E b)
    (x : SpTowerShriek.OpenExchange l E b o) (laws : SpTowerShriek.Laws l E b o x)
    (q : Coordinates l E b) (z : FiniteCoordinates l E) :
    ∃ finiteData : FiniteNormalization l E k b o q z,
    ∃ ops : CompositionOperations l E k b o q z,
    ∀ h : Preservation l E k b o q,
    ∃ et : EtaleCalculus l E k b o q z,
      Nonempty (CompositionCoherence l E k b o q z h finiteData ops) ∧
      (∀ {U X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [U.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (U ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (U ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (U ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (j : U ⟶ X) [j.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (a : Compactification j) (c : Compactification f) (K : C l E b q U),
    (ops.composition j f (j ≫ f) rfl a c (c.precomp j)).hom.app K =
      (F l E b o q c).map
        ((et.etale_shriek j a).hom.app K ≫
          (openEtaleCoordinates l E b o q z j (et.etale j)).hom.app K.obj) ≫
        (openComposition l E b o q j c).hom.app K.obj)
